action.action-desc: Ms. Velázquez introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Financial Services

form.official-title: To apply the Truth in Lending Act to small business financing, to regulate brokers and require the licensing of brokers, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Small Business Lending Disclosure and Broker Regulation Act of 2020.

section.header: Application of the Truth in Lending to small business financing

subsection.text: The Truth in Lending Act (15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following:

toc.toc-entry: 192. Application of this title to small business financing.

paragraph.text: The term closed-end commercial credit—

subparagraph.text: means a closed-end extension of credit, secured or unsecured, including financing with an established principal amount and including equipment financing that does not meet the definition of a lease under the Uniform Commercial Code (U.C.C.—§ 2A–103(j)) the proceeds of which the recipient does not intend to use primarily for personal, family or household purposes; and
includes financing with an established principal amount and duration.

paragraph.text: The term consumer financial product or service has the meaning given that term under section 1002 of the Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010.
The term Director means the Director of the Bureau.

The term factoring means a transaction that includes an agreement to purchase, transfer, or sell a legally enforceable claim for payment held by a recipient for goods the recipient has supplied or services the recipient has rendered that have been ordered but for which payment has not yet been made.

subparagraph.text: The term finance charge means the cost of financing as a dollar amount, and includes any charge payable directly or indirectly by the recipient of the financing and imposed directly or indirectly by the provider of the financing as an incident to or a condition of the extension of financing.

subparagraph.header: Calculation in open-end commercial credit plans
subparagraph.text: In any open-end commercial credit plan, the finance charge shall be computed assuming the maximum amount of credit available to the recipient, in each case, is drawn and repaid at the minimum rate.
In any factoring transaction, the finance charge shall include the discount taken on the face value of the accounts receivable.

In any lease financing transaction, the finance charge shall include the sum of the lease payments and, if there is a fixed-price purchase option or a purchase option with a price that can be calculated at the time of disclosure, the purchase price listed in the contract that the lessee may pay to acquire the leased goods at the end of the lease, minus—

clause.text: if the finance company selects, manufactures, or supplies the goods to be leased, the price that the finance company would sell the goods in a cash transaction; or
if the finance company does not select, manufacture, or supply the goods to be leased, the price the finance company will pay to acquire the property to be leased.

If, as a condition of obtaining the offered commercial financing the provider requires the recipient to pay off the balance of an existing loan or advance from the same provider, any prepayment charge or penalty required to be paid on the existing financing shall be included as a financing charge.

clause.header: Treatment when repayment amount is calculated as a fixed amount
clause.text: For purposes of clause (i), for financing for which the total repayment amount is calculated as a fixed amount, the prepayment charge is equal to the original finance charge multiplied by the required prepayment amount as a percentage of the total repayment amount, minus any portion of the total repayment amount forgiven by the provider at the time of prepayment.

paragraph.text: The term open-end commercial credit plan means any small business financing provided by a person under a plan in which the person reasonably contemplates repeat transactions, which prescribes the terms of such transactions, and which provides for a finance charge which may be computed from time to time on the outstanding unpaid balance.
The term provider mean a person who offers or provides small business financing.
The term recipient means a person who is presented an offer of small business financing.
The term sales-based financing—

subparagraph.text: means a transaction where there is an extension of financing to a recipient that is repaid by the recipient, over time, as a percentage of sales or revenue, in which the payment amount may increase or decrease according to the volume of sales made or revenue received by the recipient; and
includes transactions with a true-up mechanism.

paragraph.text: The term small business has the meaning given the term small-business concern under section 3 of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 632).
The term small business financing—

subparagraph.text: means any line of credit, closed-end commercial credit, sales-based financing, or other non-equity obligation or alleged obligation of a partnership, corporation, cooperative, association, or other entity that is $2,500,000 or less; and
does not include any obligation or alleged obligation of an individual that is primarily for personal, family, or household purposes.

paragraph.text: The term specific offer means the specific terms of small business financing, including price or amount, that is quoted to a recipient, based on information obtained from, or about the recipient, which, if accepted by a recipient, shall be binding on the provider, as applicable, subject to any specific requirements stated in such terms.

section.header: Application of this title to small business financing

subsection.text: This title shall apply to small business financing made to a small business to the same extent as this title applies to extensions of credit made to a consumer.
The Director shall issue such rules as may be required to carry out this chapter.

For purposes of carrying out this chapter and other Federal laws, including the Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010, the Bureau shall have the same authority with respect to small business financing as the Bureau has with respect to consumer financial products and services.

Any provider offering small business financing to a small business shall disclose the following pieces of information to a recipient at the time of extending a specific offer for small business financing:

paragraph.text: The total amount to be paid to the small business, taking into account all fees and charges to be withheld at disbursement.

subparagraph.text: With respect to closed-end commercial credit, the annual percentage rate, using only the words annual percentage rate or the abbreviation APR, expressed as a yearly rate, inclusive of any fees and finance charges that cannot be avoided by a recipient.

With respect to open-end commercial credit plans, the annual percentage rate, using only the words annual percentage rate or the abbreviation APR, expressed as a nominal yearly rate, inclusive of any fees and finance charges that cannot be avoided by a recipient, based on the maximum amount of credit available to the recipient and the term resulting from making the minimum required payments term as disclosed.

clause.text: With respect to sales-based financing, the estimated annual percentage rate, using the words annual percentage rate or the abbreviation APR, expressed as a yearly rate, inclusive of any fees and finance charges, based on the estimated term of repayment and the projected periodic payment amounts.
The estimated term of repayment and the projected periodic payment amounts shall be calculated based on the projection of the recipient’s sales, called the projected sales volume.
For purposes of clause (ii), the projected sales volume may be calculated—

subclause.text: according to a method defined by the Director based on the recipient’s historical sales volume over a defined period of time that is used for all sales-based financing transactions by that provider; or

by another method defined by the provider and approved by the Director, with ongoing monitoring by the Director for accuracy based on a comparison of the annual percentage rate as disclosed to the recipient and as calculated retrospectively upon repayment of the financing.

clause.text: With respect to factoring, the estimated annual percentage rate, using that term.
To calculate the estimated annual percentage rate under clause (i)—

subclause.text: the purchase amount shall be considered the financing amount;
the purchase amount minus the total cost of financing shall be considered the payment amount; and
the term is established by the payment due date of the receivables.

clause.text: Notwithstanding clause (ii)(III), a provider may estimate the term for a factoring transaction as the average payment period, its historical data over a period not to exceed the previous twelve months, concerning payment invoices paid by the party owing the accounts receivable in question.

paragraph.text: With respect to small business financing other than factoring—

subparagraph.text: for payment amounts that are fixed—

clause.text: the payment amounts and frequency (e.g., daily, weekly, monthly); and
if the term is longer than one month and payment frequency is other than monthly, the average total monthly payment amount; or

subparagraph.text: for payment amounts that are variable—

clause.text: a full payment schedule or a description of the method used to calculate the amounts and frequency of payments; and
if the term is longer than one month, the estimated average total monthly payment amount.

paragraph.text: For financing other than factoring, the term of the small business financing, either in months or in years, or, if the term is not fixed, the estimated term, calculated using the same assumptions used to calculate the estimated annual percentage rate.
The finance charge of the small business financing, broken down to show what expenses and fees are included in the finance charge.
In the event that a recipient elects to pay off or refinance the small business financing prior to full repayment, the provider must disclose—

subparagraph.text: whether the recipient would be required to pay any finance charges other than interest accrued since the recipient’s last payment; and

if the recipient is required to pay the finance charges described under subparagraph (A), the percentage of any unpaid portion of the finance charge and maximum dollar amount the recipient could be required to pay; and
whether the recipient would be required to pay any additional fees not already included in the finance charge.

paragraph.text: Any collateral requirement that will be imposed on the small business in connection with the small business financing.

Disclosures made pursuant to this section shall be in writing, at the time a specific offer is made, and in a manner that is clear, conspicuous, complete, and allows the small business to compare the range of small business financing options that the small business may be considering.
In making any disclosure pursuant to this section, the disclosures required under paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of subsection (a) shall be displayed most prominently.

section.text: When a lender of small business financing refinances or modifies an existing loan with a fixed fee as the primary financing charge, the lender may not charge a fee on the small business’s outstanding principal unless there is a tangible benefit to the small business.

subsection.text: Nothing in this chapter may be construed to prevent a provider from providing or disclosing additional information on a small business financing being offered to a recipient, provided however, that such additional information may not be disclosed as part of the disclosure required by this chapter.

paragraph.text: If other metrics of financing cost are disclosed or used in the application process of a small business financing, these metrics shall not be presented as a rate if they are not the annual interest rate or the annual percentage rate.
The term interest, when used to describe a percentage rate to a recipient or potential recipient, shall only be used to describe annualized percentage rates, such as the annual interest rate.

subsection.text: When a provider states in writing a rate of finance charge or a financing amount to a recipient during an application process for small business financing, the provider shall also state the annual percentage rate or, in the case of sales-based financing or factoring, the estimated annual percentage rate, with equal or greater prominence, using the term annual percentage rate or the abbreviation APR.
The table of chapters for the Truth in Lending Act is amended by adding at the end the following:

Not later than the end of the 24-month period beginning on the date of enactment of this Act, the Director of the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection shall issue final rules to carry out the amendments made by this section.
Chapter 6 of the Truth in Lending Act, as added by subsection (a), shall take effect after the end of the 36-month period beginning on the date of enactment of this Act.

section.text: Section 1013 of the Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010 (12 U.S.C. 5493) is amended by adding at the end the following:

subsection.text: There is established in the Bureau an Office of Broker Regulation, which shall be responsible for carrying out section 1018.
The Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010 (12 U.S.C. 5481 et seq.) is amended—

paragraph.text: by redesignating section 1018 as section 1019; and
by inserting after section 1017 the following:
The term broker means a natural person who—

subparagraph.text: is not a creditor or purchaser; and
solicits and presents offers of commercial financing on behalf of a third party.

paragraph.text: The term Director means the Director of the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection.
The term State means each of the several States, the District of Columbia, and the territories and possessions of the United States.
The terms small business and small business financing have the meaning given those terms under section 193 of the Truth in Lending Act.
A broker shall, in facilitating financing offered by a third-party lender for a small business—

subparagraph.text: provide the small business with a disclosure containing the information described under paragraph (2); and

educate the small business on each small business financing option and ensure that the small business reasonably understands the cost and terms of the small business financing as well as the pros and cons of the small business financing decision before the small business enters into a contract for such small business financing.

paragraph.text: Each disclosure required under paragraph (1) shall include:

subparagraph.text: A list of all small business financing options for which the small business qualifies through the broker’s services and, with respect to each such small business financing option, the disclosures described under section 193 of the Truth in Lending Act.
The lowest annual percentage rate option.
All the lenders to which the broker has sent or will send small business financing applications on the small business’s behalf.
All compensation that will be paid to the broker, including—

clause.text: all charges that will be paid directly or indirectly by the small business; and
whether such compensation paid to the broker will be paid up front or financed through the life of the small business financing.

subparagraph.text: All conflicts of interest the broker may have.
A break down and explanation of the broker’s fee structure, including—

clause.text: any financial or economic interest the broker has in offering a product to the small business; and
whether the broker will receive a higher fee for brokering a certain small business financing over another small business financing.

paragraph.header: Public disclosure of previous borrower results

subparagraph.text: Each broker shall post clearly and prominently on the website of the broker the anonymous and aggregated results of previous small business borrowers who have obtained small business financing through the broker’s services, in terms of annual percentage rate and financing product.

Notwithstanding subparagraph (A), if a broker does not have a website, the broker shall disclose the information described in subparagraph (A) in a paper format, upon request by any small business borrower.

paragraph.header: Small business complaints with respect to brokers
paragraph.text: The Director shall—

subparagraph.text: collect complaints from small businesses with respect to their experiences with brokers; and
make such complaints available to the public on the website of the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection.

paragraph.text: A broker that is paid higher fees with certain lenders, small business financing types, or through terms other than the size of the small business financing may not state that the broker is acting in the best interest of the potential small business borrower.
A loan originator or broker may not steer a small business to small business financing that is not in the small business’s best interest.

subparagraph.header: No fee if parties do not come to an agreement
subparagraph.text: A broker may not charge a small business any fee if—

clause.text: the broker is unable to find the small business financing; or
the small business chooses not to accept financing through the broker’s services.

subparagraph.text: If a broker or third-party lender offers an existing small business customer new financing, neither the broker nor the third-party lender may charge the small business a new financing charge for the financing being replaced.

paragraph.text: A person may only perform the function of a broker in a State if the person is licensed as a broker—

subparagraph.text: with respect to a State that has a covered broker licensing law, by the State; or
with respect to a State that does not have a covered broker licensing law, by the Bureau.

paragraph.text: With respect to a State, the term covered broker licensing law means a State law that the Director determines meets the following requirements:

subparagraph.text: The law provides for a process to license brokers operating in the State.
The law prohibits any person from acting as a broker in the State unless such person is licensed by the State as a broker.
The law prohibits licensing an individual as a broker if such individual—

clause.text: has had a State license revoked for cause in any State;
has had a Federal license revoked for cause; or
has been convicted of any crime involving lying, deceit, or misappropriation of the truth.

subparagraph.text: The law prohibits a broker from employing any individual, other than a clerical employee, who is described under clause (i), (ii), or (iii) of subparagraph (C).
The law requires a licensed broker to undergo State audits and provides for examination of the broker by State regulators.
With respect to any violation of a State law or regulation in connection with performing the duties of a broker, the law provides for—

clause.text: an initial warning being given to the broker;
a cure period offered to the broker during which the broker can cure the violation; and
if the broker fails to cure the violation, civil or criminal penalties which include—

subclause.text: the revocation of any broker license granted to the violator; and
a ban on the violator being granted any other professional license for a period of not less than 5 years.

subparagraph.text: The law requires the State agency in charge of licensing brokers to maintain a website that lists all disciplinary actions taken against brokers.

paragraph.text: Not later than the end of the 12-month period beginning on the date of enactment of this section, the Director shall establish a Federal broker licensing program that, to the extent practicable, meets the requirements for a covered broker licensing law described under paragraph (2).

subparagraph.text: Subsection (a) shall take effect after the end of the 2-year period beginning on the date of enactment of this section.

Notwithstanding subsection (a), a person acting as broker in a State on the date of enactment of this section who has applied for a broker license under a State covered broker licensing law (or, with respect to a State that does not have a covered broker licensing law, with the Federal broker licensing program established under paragraph (3)) may continue to act as a broker in such State while the application is pending.

subsection.text: The Director may issue such rules as may be necessary to carry out this section.

paragraph.text: Any person who violates a provision of this section shall—

subparagraph.text: be fined not less than $5,000 and not more than $72,000;
disgorge any funds or other property obtained in connection with such violation;
in the case of an individual licensed as a broker by the Bureau, have such license suspended for 1 year; and
in the case of an individual licensed as a broker by the Bureau who has violated a provision of this section previously, have such license permanently revoked.

paragraph.text: Any person who violates a provision of this section in an egregious manner shall be fined not more than $5,000,000 or imprisoned not more than 20 years, or both.
Any person employing a broker at the time the broker violates a provision of this section shall—

subparagraph.text: be fined not more than $853,062;
disgorge any funds or other property obtained in connection with such violation;
be prohibited from taking any action involving small business lending or the brokerage industry for not more than 30 business days; and

in the case of a violation that was in an egregious manner, be prohibited from taking any action involving small business lending or the brokerage industry for more than 30 business days, which may include a permanent prohibition on the person taking any action involving small business lending or the brokerage industry.

paragraph.text: If an individual has their State broker license revoked by reason of violating a State law or regulation in connection with performing the duties of a broker—

subparagraph.text: any professional license granted to the individual by the Federal Government shall be terminated; and
the individual may not receive a professional license from the Federal Government before the end of the 5-year period beginning on the date of such revocation.

paragraph.text: An action to enforce a violation of this section may also be brought by a State attorney general in any appropriate United States district court, or any other court of competent jurisdiction.
